subject: Post-call: Procurement readiness & commercial path (PO vs card / marketplace)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>, Tom Hirsch <tom.hirsch@acmecorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (procurement path)

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from my side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we agreed
- Goal: POC with Redwood for customer-facing search assistant (approx 2M tokens/month expected).
- Minimum commercial need: single-tenant reserved capacity or hosted with encryption + DPA.
- Primary constraint: procurement needs SOC 2 report + signed DPA; PO preferred but open to card for POC.

Open items / asks for Acme
1) Confirm whether procurement will require vendor SOC 2 on file vs only answers to the questionnaire (you said both may be checked).
2) Confirm payment path preference (PO vs card) for pilot vs production.
3) Any required legal clauses to flag in advance (data residency / audit rights).

What Redwood will do
- Share SOC 2 report and latest DPA (attached). (attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2024.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v3.docx)
- Fill the security questionnaire you sent and return by Thursday EOD. (attachment: Security_Questionnaire_Acme.xlsx)
- Outline commercial path: card for quick start (credit card) or PO via Net30 for production. Also note we support AWS Marketplace procurement if you prefer that route.

Next steps
- Samantha: confirm PO vs card preference for the pilot by EOD Thu (06/04).
- Marissa: share attachments and questionnaire answers by EOD Thu (06/04).
- Internal: loop in Neha (sec/compliance) and Karthik (commercial/legal) for any follow-ups.

Thanks — will follow up here with the filled questionnaire.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (procurement path)

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A couple clarifications from our procurement side: 

- For the pilot (30–60 days), we prefer to use a P-card (credit card) to avoid PO cycles. If the pilot moves to production, procurement will push for a PO / Net30 contract.
- SOC 2: Procurement wants to review the SOC 2 Type II report. We will also ask security to run the questionnaire; having both speeds approvals.
- Marketplace: We are interested in AWS Marketplace if pricing and entitlements are compatible — that can make the procurement path smoother for our finance team.

I’ll confirm the pilot payment method by Thu EOD. Please send over the SOC 2 and DPA now so I can start the review.

Samantha

—Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (procurement path)

Marissa / Samantha — I reviewed the questionnaire and prepped answers inline. High level: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as standard), the current DPA (attached), and a short technical sheet on our private deployment options / region controls.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2024.pdf (redacted), Redwood_DPA_v3.docx, Security_Questionnaire_Acme.xlsx (answered).

Quick notes on dependencies / gating items
- If Acme requires vendor-hosted logs for a compliance audit, we’ll need to scope that as it may require a dedicated retention policy (possible additional cost).
- Data residency: our Private offering can be deployed into customer VPCs for strict residency; otherwise hosted instances are in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 by default.
- Pen test evidence: we can share high-level summaries and remediation timelines; full reports need an NDA.

If procurement confirms pilot via card, we’ll treat this as a standard onboarding playbook and can start within 2 business days of signing. If they require a PO up front, legal will need to review the standard MSA which can add ~5–10 business days depending on redlines.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick commercial note: 
- Pilot pricing: recommend card-based trial at the rate we quoted on the call (Pilot SKU: RDW-PILOT-1). If they convert to reserved capacity, we’ll propose a 12-month commit with a standard volume discount (details in HubSpot).
- PO vs Marketplace: AWS Marketplace often speeds PO processing but may restrict custom contract language — if Acme needs non-standard legal terms, PO via direct MSA is still the path. Marketplace is excellent if they accept our standard terms.
- Quick asks for Marissa: please capture whether Acme needs any custom SLAs or data residency clauses so Legal can scope the MSA.
